tier_1_backbone.description: Always-on latents that fire at ~100% frequency across every illness group and dataset. Not disease-discriminative. Likely encode low-level or domain-level features such as 'this is a chest X-ray image'. Despite appearing #1/#2 in raw top-k rankings per illness, their AUROC is near chance and they should be excluded from clinical interpretability claims.

latents.interpretation: Global chest X-ray presence feature. Uniform across all illness groups and datasets. Acts as a bias/intercept term in the feature space.
Global chest X-ray presence feature. Nearly identical profile to 3512. Likely redundant with it.
Universal backbone feature with no illness specificity.
Universal backbone feature with no illness specificity.

Universal backbone feature with no illness specificity.

tier_2_healthy_lung_detectors.description: Latents that fire most strongly for 'no_finding' (healthy) images and are suppressed when pathology is present. High AUROC because they reliably distinguish normal from abnormal. These encode a 'healthy lung' signal rather than a specific disease.

latents.interpretation: Strong healthy-lung detector. Fires at 98% frequency and very high activation for 'no_finding' across all datasets. Activation drops 40-60% for all pathological groups. Likely encodes normal lung parenchymal texture or aeration. Consistent across CheXpert, SIIM-COVID, and TB — qualifies as a universally learned healthy-lung feature.

Strongest universal discriminator overall (AUROC=0.843 on SIIM-COVID). Fires preferentially and strongly for healthy images; suppressed for sick patients. Pattern is consistent across all three datasets with non-NaN AUROC. The SIIM-COVID result is especially strong, suggesting this latent captures features that clearly separate COVID-positive from COVID-negative chest X-rays.
Secondary healthy-lung detector. Very similar profile to 818 but weaker on TB. Also a top-k latent for no_finding by z-score standout (Δ=125 vs other illness groups).

tier_3_pathology_presence_detectors.description: Latents that fire strongly for sick patients and are suppressed for healthy images. The opposite polarity to tier-2. These encode general 'something is wrong' signals rather than specific conditions.

latents.interpretation: Strong pathology-presence detector with near-perfect inverse of the healthy-lung pattern. Only fires on 18-32% of healthy images vs 47-70% of sick images. Especially specific to airspace opacity and pleural abnormality. TB AUROC 0.668 and SIIM 0.779 confirm cross-dataset universality. The top standout latent for airspace_opacity (Δ=81.1 above other illnesses).

Disease-group-specific pathology detector with highest CheXpert AUROC (0.642). Peaks strongly for pleural abnormality and atelectasis. Cross-activates for vascular edema. Suggests this latent encodes fluid-related lung changes. Also the top standout for both pleural_abnormality and atelectasis by z-score.

Cardiac/vascular pathology detector. Peaks for cardiac_mediastinal and vascular_edema — conditions involving enlarged heart or pulmonary vasculature. Low on TB (0.522) suggests this is less relevant for TB's typical presentation (which is more parenchymal). Top standout latent for cardiac_mediastinal.

tier_4_illness_specific.description: Latents with the highest z-score differential for a specific illness group relative to all others. These are the most interpretable disease-specific features.

latents.note: See tier_2 — also the top no_finding standout

latents.interpretation: Pleural/atelectasis feature — may encode pleural thickening or fluid-related density changes
Cardiomegaly/mediastinal widening feature; shared activation with vascular edema is clinically expected (cardiac failure causes both)

latents.note: Appears in both airspace_opacity and no_finding standouts — may encode a texture that spans normal aeration and mild opacity
Shared pleural-atelectasis feature — clinically consistent with atelectasis causing pleural effusion

shared_latents_pleural_atelectasis.interpretation: Clinically expected overlap — atelectasis (collapsed lung) and pleural abnormality often co-occur and share imaging features like increased lung density and reduced volume.

shared_latents_cardiac_vascular.interpretation: Clinically expected overlap — cardiac failure causes both enlarged mediastinum and pulmonary vascular edema; the SAE learned this physical co-occurrence.

spatial_grounding.issue: pearson_r is NaN for all 7056 entries despite n_images > 0 for 504 entries. The correlation between patch-level latent activations and disease region masks was never computed — likely a pipeline bug (possible failure in loading segmentation masks or correlation computation).
spatial_grounding.impact: Cannot make claims about spatial localization of these latents.

fine_probe_labels.status: NaN for all CheXpert and TB labels; near-random for RSNA pneumonia
fine_probe_labels.issue: The per-label fine discriminability probe (Atelectasis, Cardiomegaly, Edema, etc.) produced all NaN on CheXpert and TB. Only RSNA 'pneumonia' label has values but all ~0.49-0.51 (chance level). Fine-grained per-label discrimination cannot be reported.
fine_probe_labels.impact: Cannot map latents to specific CheXpert label categories.

rsna_coarse_probe.issue: RSNA is a binary pneumonia dataset; the coarse illness-group probe requires multi-class labels. No coarse AUROC is available for RSNA.
rsna_coarse_probe.impact: RSNA contributes no discriminability signal to the analysis.
